qs.q: A patient with chronic severe peptic ulcers and diarrhoea is suspected of having Zollinger-Ellison syndrome. Which laboratory test should be ordered to confirm this diagnosis?
qs.e: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is caused by a gastrin-secreting tumour that leads to excessive gastric acid, diagnosed by checking elevated serum gastrin levels. Stool cultures are used for identifying infectious diarrhoea rather than endocrine tumours.

qs.q: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is caused by a gastrinoma presenting with
o: Recurrent peptic ulcers in atypical locations due to excess gastrin secretion.
Necrolytic migratory erythema together with diabetes mellitus.
Episodes of hypoglycaemia accompanied by seizures.
Flushing, diarrhoea, and right‑sided heart disease.
qs.e: Pancreatic/duodenal gastrinoma → massive acid hypersecretion → ulcers including 4th duodenum and jejunum. ~25% associated with MEN1.

qs.q: Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is characterized by Hypergastrinemia. This leads to:
o: Hypochlorhydria due to parietal cell loss
Severe peptic ulcers due to excessive acid secretion
qs.e: A gastrin-secreting tumor (gastrinoma) leads to excessive HCl production, causing multiple, severe peptic ulcers.
